493e39e1181cbcdfa3f77d430e50da4eb92934dc.full_text: Why do healthy swimmers drown in cold water in under sixty seconds? Most people assume hypothermia is the killer, but hypothermia takes thirty minutes to set in. The immediate killer is cold shock response. When freezing water strikes your skin, skin thermoreceptors trigger an involuntary gasp reflex. If your mouth is underwater when you gasp, you instantly inhale up to two liters of water into your lungs. Your blood pressure spikes instantly as peripheral veins contract, risking cardiac arrest. To survive, fight the instinct to swim: float on your back for ninety seconds until your breathing regulates. A vital reflex to master, before sudden immersion steals your breath...

a3951742036f7d8450c866075858160863f43131.full_text: Have you ever noticed that almost no national flag in the world uses the color purple? It isn't because world leaders hated the color. Until the mid-nineteenth century, purple dye was made exclusively from the slime of thousands of sea snails. It took ten thousand snails to produce just a single gram of purple dye, making it literally worth more than its weight in pure gold. Only royalty could afford purple clothes, and no country could afford a purple flag. Today, synthetic dye is cheap, but flags kept their traditional colors. Within a week, thirty more joined her; within a month, over four hundred people were dancing in the square. City physicians believed hot blood was the cause, and hired musicians to keep them moving. Dozens collapsed from heart attacks, dehydration, and sheer physical exhaustion. Modern historians believe it was mass psychogenic illness triggered by famine and rye mold ergot poisoning.
